title: Flame spread over PMMA in low-velocity microgravity flow
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents a study of opposed-flow flame spread over a flat PMMA sample in microgravity.
key_findings: Flame spread rate decreased as opposed-flow velocity decreased below 10 cm/s
A low-velocity quenching limit was observed near 2 cm/s
ai_summary: [MOCK] Opposed-flow flame spread over PMMA in microgravity slows as ventilation velocity drops, with quenching near 2 cm/s.
rationale: [MOCK] Directly constrains flame-spread limits for a common cabin material across the ventilation range used on orbit.
mission_implications: Informs material screening and minimum ventilation assumptions for cabin interior design.

title: Smoldering propagation in polyurethane foam under microgravity
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents a study of smoldering front propagation in porous foam without buoyant flow.
key_findings: Smoldering front propagated without visible flame
Front speed was sensitive to oxygen concentration
ai_summary: [MOCK] Smoldering can propagate through foam in microgravity with no flame signature, complicating detection.
rationale: [MOCK] Smoldering without flame defeats optical flame detectors and is a known cabin fire hazard.
mission_implications: Argues for smoke and CO sensing rather than flame-only detection in crewed modules.

title: Low-velocity extinction limits of a methane diffusion flame
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents drop-tower measurement of blow-off limits for a gaseous diffusion flame.
key_findings: Extinction strain rate decreased with reduced gravity
Flame sustained at velocities below terrestrial blow-off limits
ai_summary: [MOCK] Microgravity flames survive at lower flow velocities than terrestrial blow-off limits predict.
rationale: [MOCK] Changes the assumed velocity threshold at which a flame self-extinguishes in a cabin.
mission_implications: Ventilation shutdown as a fire response must account for wider microgravity stability limits.

title: Wire insulation flammability in oxygen-enriched atmosphere
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents a study of insulation flammability at elevated oxygen fraction.
key_findings: Ignition delay fell sharply above 28 percent oxygen
Drip behaviour differed from terrestrial tests
ai_summary: [MOCK] Elevated oxygen fraction markedly shortens ignition delay for ETFE wire insulation.
rationale: [MOCK] Quantifies a material limit that depends on cabin oxygen fraction, a controllable design parameter.
mission_implications: Supports caps on oxygen fraction or stricter insulation screening in high-O2 cabins.

title: Aerosol detector response to microgravity smoke particle size
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents detector response testing across short microgravity periods.
key_findings: Particle size distribution shifted toward larger agglomerates
ai_summary: [MOCK] Microgravity smoke agglomerates differently, so terrestrial detector thresholds under-report.
rationale: [MOCK] Detector calibration directly affects time-to-alarm for a cabin fire.
mission_implications: Detector thresholds should be re-derived from microgravity aerosol data, not terrestrial standards.

title: Carbon dioxide suppression of a microgravity flame
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents a suppression test measuring agent concentration needed to extinguish a gaseous flame.
key_findings: Required agent concentration exceeded terrestrial values
Extinguishment time increased without buoyant mixing
ai_summary: [MOCK] More suppressant is needed in microgravity because there is no buoyant mixing to distribute it.
rationale: [MOCK] Sets the sizing basis for portable extinguishers carried in crewed vehicles.
mission_implications: Extinguisher agent mass and discharge duration must be sized for mixing-limited conditions.

title: Ventilation effects on flame stability in a sealed cabin volume
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents a study of how cabin airflow patterns alter flame stability.
key_findings: Local flow acceleration lengthened the flame
Stagnation zones sustained flames longer than predicted
ai_summary: [MOCK] Cabin airflow patterns, not just bulk velocity, determine where flames persist in microgravity.
rationale: [MOCK] Links ventilation design to flame persistence, a directly actionable cabin layout constraint.
mission_implications: Airflow surveys should identify stagnation zones that could harbour sustained flames.

title: Screening candidate cabin materials for microgravity flammability
abstract: [MOCK] Synthetic record for local development. Not a real citation. Represents a comparative screening of several polymer coupons under short microgravity exposure.
key_findings: Two of six coupons failed to self-extinguish
Ranking of materials differed from terrestrial results
ai_summary: [MOCK] Material rankings from terrestrial tests do not transfer reliably to microgravity screening.
rationale: [MOCK] Material selection is the primary preventive control against cabin fire.
mission_implications: Cabin material qualification should include microgravity screening, not terrestrial pass/fail alone.
